A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–E. Content can be matched reliably despite pagination and equation-number changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations using Gaussian data, MNIST, and a nonlinear ring-position task, including additional supervised-network results in Appendix E and Figure S1.

after.justification: V2 retains these original simulations and their reported outcomes in Sections 4–5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The Oja, Similarity Matching, autoencoder, and supervised two-layer architectures and learning procedures remain unchanged. Revisions concern their mathematical analysis rather than model components or training algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian-data tasks, nonlinear ring-position reconstruction, and MNIST experiments. Appendix E retains the same supervised-network scenarios.

E2.justification: The architecture comparisons in Figures 3 and 5 and the learning-noise versus Gaussian synaptic-noise comparison in Figure 6 retain the same participants. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Experimental settings remain unchanged, including online learning, batch size one for SGD, MNIST preprocessing, network dimensions, learning rates, and drift measurements. The settings accompanying Figure S1 also match.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same learning-rate, variance, and dimensionality sweeps, nonlinear receptive-field analysis, and synaptic-noise comparisons. Figure S1's analyses of task rank and output dimension are unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-sampling and uncertainty descriptions match. These include Figure 4's 80 runs and five sampled angles, its standard-error bands, and the standard-deviation reporting in Figures 5 and 6.

E6.justification: All seven figure images are identical across versions, and their result descriptions match. Reported drift trends and final diffusion-rate expressions are retained; no experimental result is added, removed, or numerically revised.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the inconsistent perturbation variable in Eq. 26 from delta W to N. Appendix C.1.1 changes the positive-sign updates to delta n = -Hn and delta pi = -Lambda pi, now Eqs. 41–42. These are localized mathematical corrections; the framework and final diffusion formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and discussion retain the same central claims: task-irrelevant stimuli induce representational drift across learning rules, with dependencies and geometry distinct from Gaussian synaptic noise.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly explains Similarity Matching's non-curl-free dynamics and possible coupling between normal and tangent perturbations, motivating non-orthogonal projections in Section 3.1 and Appendix C.1.1. Empirical interpretations and the limitations in Section 6 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Simulation parameters, data-processing descriptions, computing-resource acknowledgments, and the code-availability statement are retained. The expanded derivation adds no implementation or reproducibility settings.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 41 works and retain the same research positioning. New citation callouts in Section 3.1 reference already cited works; the exchange of reference numbers 29 and 30 adds no literature.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify Section 3.1 and Appendices B–C, replacing inappropriate Hessian terminology with Jacobian language and renaming corresponding subsections. Appendix E gains a 'Supervised' heading qualifier. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from page 7 to page 8, and Figure S1 moves to page 26 with larger caption text. Appendix C converts two inline updates into numbered display equations. Figure artwork and plotted content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical precision through the Eq. 26 correction, the negative-sign updates in Appendix C.1.1, and clearer treatment of Jacobians and non-orthogonal projections. These localized corrections make the analysis easier to follow, while the empirical evidence and central conclusions remain unchanged.
